cards.name: Keyboard Shortcuts & Menus
cards.summary: Opens the Keyboard Shortcuts and Menus dialog, where you reassign or clear keyboard shortcuts for menu commands, panel menus and tools, and hide or colour-code menu items. It changes the application's UI only, not the open document. Enabled with or without a document open.
cards.how: Keyboard Shortcuts tab: pick a Set (Photoshop Defaults or a saved .kys set), choose Shortcuts For (Application Menus, Panel Menus, Tools, Taskspaces), click a command and type the new key; Photoshop warns when the key is already taken. Use Legacy Undo Shortcuts and Use Legacy Channel Shortcuts restore older behaviour, and Summarize exports the whole set as an HTML list. Menus tab: toggle the eye to hide a menu item or give it a colour; menu sets save as .mnu. Save the set under a new name rather than editing Photoshop Defaults.
use_for: giving a one-key shortcut to a command used hundreds of times in a product cut-out or retouching batch
colour-coding or hiding menu items so a junior designer finds the brand-approved export and colour commands
exporting the shortcut list (Summarize) as a reference sheet for a team using the same Photoshop setup
moving a custom shortcut set to a new machine via its .kys file
avoid: automating a repeated multi-step job: record an Action and give it a function key instead
overwriting Photoshop Defaults: save a named set so the defaults can be restored
expecting the change in Illustrator or CorelDRAW: each app keeps its own shortcut set
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('customization')) opens the Keyboard Shortcuts and Menus dialog (verified live 2026-10-04). No known route sets a shortcut or hides a menu item without the dialog.

review.changes: none: dialog, customization route, partial scriptable and AI/CDR equivalents match the batch and the counterpart cards

cards.name: Lock Workspace
cards.summary: A toggle that locks the panel layout: while it is checked, panels and the toolbar cannot be dragged, docked, undocked or regrouped, so the workspace cannot be rearranged by accident. Documents are unaffected. Enabled with or without a document open.
use_for: keeping a carefully arranged retouching or layout workspace from being knocked apart by a stray drag during long sessions
protecting the panel layout on a shared or pen-tablet workstation where accidental panel drags are common
avoid: rearranging or docking panels: uncheck Lock Workspace first
saving the layout for later: locking does not save anything, use Window/Workspace/New Workspace
undoing an already messed-up layout: use Window/Workspace/Reset Essentials (Reset <workspace>)
cards.script_api: No script route found by the harvest (no menuItemType or AM event matches). UXP (unverified): require('photoshop').core.performMenuCommand({commandID: 2939}); ExtendScript app.runMenuItem(2939) is not expected to work: the harvest audit found runMenuItem refuses menuBarInfo command ids (it tried 1017, 1192, 1135, not this one).

review.changes: script_api: 'runMenuItem refuses this numeric id' overstated the audit (it tried 1017/1192/1135 only); summary: dropped the unsupported claim that panels still open, close and collapse while locked

cards.name: New Workspace
cards.summary: Opens the New Workspace dialog, which saves the current panel arrangement under a name; the saved workspace then appears in Window > Workspace and in the workspace switcher so the layout can be recalled in one click. Enabled with or without a document open.
cards.how: Type a Name. Panel locations are always saved; under Capture, tick Keyboard Shortcuts, Menus and/or Toolbar to store the current shortcut set, menu set and toolbar customisation with it. Saving under an existing name overwrites that workspace.
use_for: saving a retouching layout (Layers, Properties, Histogram, Channels) separate from a typography or social-post layout
storing a task layout together with its custom shortcuts so switching jobs switches both
building a clean presentation layout for screen-recording a design walkthrough
avoid: fixing a layout that drifted: use Window/Workspace/Reset Essentials (Reset <workspace>)
stopping panels from being moved: use Window/Workspace/Lock Workspace
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('saveWorkspace')) opens the New Workspace dialog (verified live 2026-10-04). No verified route saves a workspace without the dialog.

review.changes: script_api: removed the select-workspace-by-name descriptor (slct/workspace keys are not in the batch and it switches workspaces, a sibling item's job, not New Workspace's)

cards.name: Reset Essentials
cards.summary: Restores the active workspace to its saved panel layout, putting moved, closed or resized panels back where the workspace stores them. The title follows the active workspace (it reads Reset Essentials when Essentials is active, Reset <name> otherwise); documents are unaffected. Enabled with or without a document open.
use_for: recovering a missing Layers or Properties panel, or a toolbar dragged off-screen, before a deadline
returning a shared workstation to the standard layout at the start of a design session
avoid: keeping layout changes you like: save them first with Window/Workspace/New Workspace, because reset discards them
restoring default preferences or tool settings: reset only restores the workspace's saved layout (and whatever shortcuts, menus or toolbar that workspace captured), not Preferences or tool options
preventing the layout from drifting in the first place: use Window/Workspace/Lock Workspace
cards.script_api: No script route found (the harvest did not run it: it resets the user's workspace layout, persistent UI). UXP (unverified): require('photoshop').core.performMenuCommand({commandID: 5117}); ExtendScript app.runMenuItem(5117) is not expected to work: the harvest audit found runMenuItem refuses menuBarInfo command ids (it tried 1017, 1192, 1135, not this one).

review.changes: script_api: 'runMenuItem refuses this numeric id' overstated the audit (it tried 1017/1192/1135 only); avoid: 'reset only touches panel layout' ignored workspaces saved with captured shortcuts, menus or toolbar
